overview: The Medford Historical Commission determined that 314 Winthrop Street is not historically significant, voted to support the creation of the South Street Local Historic District, and reviewed several ongoing preservation projects.

items.title: 69 Court Street Update
items.summary: Chair Ryan Hayward noted that the proposal for 69 Court Street appears abandoned and will likely be removed from future agendas.

items.title: 314 Winthrop Street Determination of Significance
items.summary: The commission voted 5-0 that 314 Winthrop Street is not significant, while the developer agreed to consult informally with commissioners on sympathetic exterior design elements.

items.title: 48-64 Commercial Street Site Plan Review
items.summary: The commission offered no official comments on the proposed Fellsway Innovation Center commercial lab project.

items.title: Walkling Court Section 106 Review
items.summary: Commissioners discussed a state response passing federal environmental review authority to HUD and agreed to advocate for photo documentation and interpretive mitigation before site demolition.

items.title: South Street Local Historic District
items.summary: The commission voted 5-0 to send a letter of support for the proposed South Street Local Historic District as it advances to the Planning Board and City Council.

items.title: Historic District Commission Personnel Update
items.summary: Chair Ryan Hayward reported on leadership resignations at the Historic District Commission and noted his appointment as a compliance officer to assist the board.

items.title: Old Business and Project Updates
items.summary: The commission reviewed updates on demolition delay sites, grant applications for Cross Street Cemetery restoration and archaeological trenching, Thomas Brooks Park funding, and neighborhood survey forms for Bradley Hall Estates and Fulton Heights.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: The commission voted 5-0 to approve the previous meeting minutes.
